Notes

Version 13. Only your four picks are kept (you: "discard ships that I didnt want"). Each is one grown structure (Ship Design Bible, chapter 14): one body, its prongs, lance, hood, blade and rail split from the body's own section.

Its hull detail is modelled over it in Blender and baked onto its own UVs, never tiled (chapter 15). Primary armour plates cut along swept and raked lines, every station its own, each plate raised by its own amount, the big ones with a second plate laid over them; a thinner sub-armour layer beneath; in the gaps and trenches the machinery of the under layer. A smooth dome in a collar, held by straps; a round fan vent with a ring of lamps; shaped vents (chevrons and raked slots) with slanted slats; lamps, the red eye in its housing; green liveries. Mirrored about the centreline, nothing repeated, lit by a low sun with its cast shadows and deep occlusion (you: "no repeating elemnts, single axis symmetry, and lots of shading to give the armor depth").

None is drawn from the species' body (chapter 13).
